subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 7 - Designated Partners Requirement & Residency
question: Apex Advisors LLP has 4 partners: Two are individuals (one an Indian citizen residing in Dubai who stayed in India for 80 days in FY 2023-24, and one a French national residing in India for 195 days in FY 2023-24), and two are body corporates. Who can be appointed as Designated Partners under Section 7 of the LLP Act, 2008 (as amended)?
options: Every LLP must have at least two designated partners who are individuals and at least one of them shall be a resident in India (stayed in India for not less than 120 days during the financial year); the French national qualifies as resident in India.
Only Indian citizens can be appointed as designated partners; foreign nationals are strictly barred.
Designated partners can only be corporate entities through their managing directors.
Residency requires a minimum stay of 182 days during the immediately preceding seven years.
ref: Section 7(1) of LLP Act 2008 read with amended Explanation by LLP (Amendment) Act 2021
explanation: Under Section 7(1), every LLP shall have at least two designated partners who are individuals and at least one of them shall be a resident in India. Under the LLP (Amendment) Act 2021, 'resident in India' means a person who has stayed in India for a period of not less than 120 days during the financial year. Citizenship is not required. Since the French national stayed 195 days (≥ 120 days), he satisfies the residency requirement.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 26 & 27 - Extent of Liability of LLP & Partner as Agent
question: Mr. Dave, a partner in Zenith Logistics LLP, entered into a supply contract with a vendor for ₹25 Lakhs in the ordinary course of the business of the LLP. However, under the internal registered LLP Agreement, partners' borrowing/contracting power was capped at ₹10 Lakhs without prior approval of all partners. The vendor was unaware of this internal restriction. Is the LLP bound by the contract under Section 27?
options: Yes, the LLP is liable because a partner is an agent of the LLP, and the LLP is bound unless the partner had no authority and the third party knew that he had no authority or did not believe him to be a partner.
No, the contract is ultra vires the LLP Agreement and completely void ab initio.
Mr. Dave alone is personally liable for the full ₹25 Lakhs, and the LLP is completely exempt.
The contract is enforceable only up to ₹10 Lakhs, and balance ₹15 Lakhs is unenforceable.
ref: Section 27(1) and 27(2) of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008
explanation: Under Section 27(2), an LLP is liable for an obligation arising from a contract or otherwise in the course of its business. Under Section 27(1), an LLP is not bound by anything done by a partner in dealing with a person if: (a) the partner in fact has no authority to act for the LLP; AND (b) the person knows that he has no authority or does not know or believe him to be a partner. Since the vendor had no knowledge of the internal limit, the LLP is bound.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 30 - Unlimited Liability in Case of Fraud
question: In Horizon Infotech LLP, partner Mr. Singhania, with the active knowledge and connivance of partner Mr. Gupta, carried on the business of the LLP with intent to defraud creditors by diverting funds to offshore personal accounts. Partner Ms. Roy had no knowledge and acted in good faith. What is the extent of liability under Section 30?
options: The liability of the LLP, Mr. Singhania, and Mr. Gupta shall be unlimited for all debts, while the liability of innocent partner Ms. Roy remains limited to her capital contribution.
All partners, including innocent partner Ms. Roy, incur unlimited personal liability jointly and severally.
The LLP cannot be held liable for criminal acts of its partners, making only Mr. Singhania personally liable.
Liability is limited to twice the capital contribution of each partner under the LLP Act.
ref: Section 30(1) and 30(2) of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008
explanation: Under Section 30(1), in the event of an act carried out by an LLP or any of its partners with intent to defraud creditors, the liability of the LLP and the partners who acted with intent to defraud shall be unlimited. However, under the proviso, where any partner has acted fraudulently, the LLP is liable to the same extent as the partner unless it is established that the act was done without the knowledge or authority of the LLP. An innocent partner without connivance retains limited liability.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 29 - Doctrine of Holding Out
question: Mr. Mehta, who was never a partner in Quantum Tech LLP, represented himself as a partner on social media and at a commercial trade fair. Relying on this representation, a bank granted a loan of ₹40 Lakhs to the LLP. When the LLP defaulted, the bank sued Mr. Mehta. What is Mr. Mehta's liability under Section 29?
options: Mr. Mehta is liable by holding out to the bank who has on the faith of such representation given credit to the LLP.
Mr. Mehta incurs no liability because his name was not registered in the Ministry of Corporate Affairs LLP portal.
Mr. Mehta is only liable to pay a criminal fine of ₹10,000 to the Registrar.
The bank loses its claim because it failed to inspect the public register of partners.
ref: Section 29(1) of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008
explanation: Under Section 29(1) (Doctrine of Holding Out), anyone who by words spoken or written or by conduct represents himself, or knowingly permits himself to be represented to be a partner in an LLP, is liable to any person who has on the faith of any such representation given credit to the LLP, whether the person representing himself does or does not know that the representation has reached the creditor.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 34 - Maintenance of Books of Account & Solvency Statement
question: Every LLP is required to prepare a Statement of Account and Solvency under Section 34(2). Within what period from the closure of each financial year must this statement be prepared and filed with the Registrar in Form 8?
options: Prepared within 6 months from the end of the financial year (by Sept 30) and filed with ROC within 30 days from the end of 6 months (i.e., by October 30).
Prepared and filed within 60 days from the end of the financial year (by May 30).
Prepared within 30 days and filed along with annual return by November 30.
Mandatory only for LLPs having capital contribution exceeding ₹1 Crore.
ref: Section 34(2) and 34(3) read with Rule 24 of LLP Rules, 2009
explanation: Under Section 34(2) read with Rule 24(4), every LLP shall prepare a Statement of Account and Solvency in Form 8 within a period of 6 months from the end of each financial year (by Sept 30) and file the same with the Registrar within 30 days from the end of 6 months of the financial year (by Oct 30).

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 34(4) - Mandatory Audit of LLP Accounts Threshold
question: Under Rule 24 of the Limited Liability Partnership Rules, 2009, an LLP is exempt from mandatory audit of its accounts if it satisfies which of the following criteria?
options: Its turnover does not exceed ₹40 Lakhs in any financial year AND its contribution does not exceed ₹25 Lakhs.
Its turnover does not exceed ₹1 Crore AND its contribution does not exceed ₹50 Lakhs.
Its turnover does not exceed ₹2 Crores regardless of contribution.
All LLPs are mandatorily required to be audited by a Chartered Accountant without exemption.
ref: Rule 24(8) of the Limited Liability Partnership Rules, 2009
explanation: Under Rule 24(8), an LLP whose turnover does not exceed, in any financial year, forty lakh rupees, or whose contribution does not exceed twenty-five lakh rupees, is not required to get its accounts audited. If either threshold is crossed (turnover > ₹40L or contribution > ₹25L), statutory audit by a CA in practice is mandatory.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 35 - Annual Return of LLP
question: Under Section 35(1) of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, every LLP shall file an annual return with the Registrar in Form 11 within what timeframe?
options: Within 60 days of closure of its financial year (i.e., by May 30).
Within 30 days of closure of its financial year (i.e., by April 30).
Within 180 days of closure of financial year (by September 30).
Simultaneously with the Statement of Account and Solvency on October 30.
ref: Section 35(1) of the LLP Act, 2008 read with Rule 25 of LLP Rules, 2009
explanation: Under Section 35(1) and Rule 25(1), every LLP shall file an annual return duly authenticated with the Registrar within 60 days of closure of its financial year in Form 11. For financial year ending March 31, the due date is May 30.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 6 - Minimum Number of Partners & Sole Partner Liability
question: Kestrel Solutions LLP had two partners, Mr. Roy and Mr. Sen. On August 1, 2023, Mr. Sen died in an accident. Mr. Roy continued carrying on the business of the LLP as the sole partner until March 31, 2024 (8 months) without admitting a new partner. Under Section 6(2), what is Mr. Roy's legal liability for debts contracted after February 1, 2024?
options: Mr. Roy is personally liable for the obligations of the LLP incurred during that period after the expiry of 6 months (i.e., from February 1 onwards).
The LLP stands automatically dissolved on the date of death of Mr. Sen with zero liability for Mr. Roy.
Mr. Roy's liability remains strictly limited to his capital contribution under all circumstances.
Mr. Roy must pay a fine of ₹50,000 but incurs no personal liability for business debts.
ref: Section 6(2) of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008
explanation: Under Section 6(2), if at any time the number of partners of an LLP is reduced below two and the LLP carries on business for more than six months while the number is so reduced, the person who has the only partner of the LLP during the time that it so carries on business after those six months and has the knowledge of the fact that it is carrying on business with him alone, shall be liable personally for the obligations of the LLP incurred during that period.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 58 & Schedule III - Conversion of Private Company into LLP
question: Starling Technologies Pvt. Ltd. wishes to convert into an LLP under Section 56 read with the Third Schedule. Which of the following conditions is mandatory for such conversion?
options: All the shareholders of the company must become partners of the LLP and no one else, and there must be no subsisting security interest in its assets at the date of application.
The conversion must be approved by the Reserve Bank of India.
The company must have paid dividends consistently for the past 3 financial years.
The company must have a minimum turnover of ₹5 Crores.
ref: Section 56 read with Third Schedule (Paragraph 2 & 3) of LLP Act, 2008
explanation: Under Paragraph 2 of the Third Schedule to the LLP Act 2008, a private company may convert into an LLP only if: (a) there is no security interest in its assets subsisting or in force at the time of application; and (b) the partners of the LLP to which it converts comprise all the shareholders of the company and no one else.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 64 - Circumstances in which LLP may be Wound Up by Tribunal
question: Under Section 64 of the LLP Act, 2008, which of the following is NOT a ground on which the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) may wind up an LLP?
options: The LLP decides to distribute its profits in equal proportion rather than according to capital contribution.
The LLP is unable to pay its debts.
The number of partners of the LLP is reduced below two for a period of more than six months.
The LLP has made a default in filing with the Registrar the Statement of Account and Solvency or annual return for any five consecutive financial years.
ref: Section 64 of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008
explanation: Under Section 64, an LLP may be wound up by Tribunal if: (a) LLP decides it be wound up; (b) number of partners reduced below 2 for >6 months; (c) LLP unable to pay debts; (d) acted against sovereignty/security of India; (e) default in filing Statement of Account & Solvency or Annual Return for 5 consecutive years; or (f) just and equitable ground. Profit sharing ratios are determined by the agreement and is not a winding up ground.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 23 - LLP Agreement & First Schedule Fallback
question: Three professionals incorporate an LLP without entering into a formal written LLP Agreement. In the absence of an agreement, how are the mutual rights and duties of the partners determined under Section 23(4)?
options: Determined by the default provisions set out in the First Schedule to the LLP Act, 2008 (including equal sharing of capital and profits, no remuneration, and equal rights in management).
Determined according to the provisions of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932.
The LLP is deemed illegal and dissolved by ROC immediately.
The oldest partner has absolute power to dictate all management affairs.
ref: Section 23(4) read with the First Schedule of the LLP Act, 2008
explanation: Under Section 23(4), in the absence of agreement as to any matter, the mutual rights and duties of the partners and the mutual rights and duties of the LLP and the partners shall be determined by the provisions relating to that matter as set out in the First Schedule. Under First Schedule, all partners share equally in capital, profits, and management with no partner entitled to remuneration.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 24 - Cessation of Partnership Interest
question: Under Section 24(1) of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, how may a partner resign or cease to be a partner in an LLP in the absence of an agreement?
options: By giving a notice in writing of not less than 30 days to the other partners of his intention to resign as partner.
By publishing a public notice in two national newspapers 60 days in advance.
A partner can never resign until all existing liabilities are fully repaid.
Only by obtaining an order of discharge from the NCLT.
ref: Section 24(1) of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008
explanation: Under Section 24(1), a person may cease to be a partner of an LLP in accordance with an agreement with the other partners or, in the absence of agreement with the other partners as to cessation of being a partner, by giving a notice in writing of not less than thirty days to the other partners of his intention to resign as partner.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 25 - Registration of Changes in Partners
question: When a person becomes or ceases to be a partner in an LLP, or changes his name or address, within what period must the LLP file notice with the Registrar in Form 4 under Section 25(2)?
options: Within 30 days from the date he becomes or ceases to be a partner or changes his name/address.
Within 15 days from the date of the partner's resignation.
Within 60 days along with the annual return.
At the end of the financial year on March 31.
ref: Section 25(2) of the LLP Act, 2008 read with Rule 21
explanation: Under Section 25(2), an LLP shall: (a) where a person becomes or ceases to be a partner, file a notice with the Registrar within thirty days from the date he becomes or ceases to be a partner; and (b) where there is any change in the name or address of a partner, file a notice with the Registrar within thirty days of such change in Form 4.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 31 - Whistle Blowing Protection in LLP
question: An employee of Orion Biotech LLP provides vital documents to the Registrar disclosing fraudulent diversion of government research grants by the designated partners. The designated partners immediately terminate the employee's services. What protection is available to the whistleblower under Section 31 of the LLP Act, 2008?
options: No partner or employee of any LLP may be discharged, demoted, suspended, threatened, harassed or in any other manner discriminated against for providing information or assisting in an investigation.
The LLP Act provides protection only to partners, not employees.
The employee is only entitled to 3 months severance pay without reinstatement.
Whistleblower protection applies exclusively to listed companies under SEBI regulations.
ref: Section 31(2) of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008
explanation: Under Section 31(2) (Whistle Blowing), no partner or employee of any LLP may be discharged, demoted, suspended, threatened, harassed or in any other manner discriminated against the terms and conditions of his LLP or employment merely because of his providing information or causing information to be provided pursuant to subsection (1).

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 60 - Compromise or Arrangement by LLP
question: Under Section 60 of the LLP Act, 2008, where a compromise or arrangement is proposed between an LLP and its creditors or partners, what majority is required at the meeting convened by the Tribunal to sanction the scheme?
options: A majority in number representing three-fourths in value of the creditors or partners present and voting in person or by proxy, and sanctioned by the Tribunal.
A simple majority of total creditors by value.
Unanimous consent of all registered partners.
Approval by 90% of secured creditors only.
ref: Section 60(2) of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008
explanation: Under Section 60(2), if a majority in number representing three-fourths in value of creditors, or partners, as the case may be, present and voting either in person or by proxy at the meeting, agree to any compromise or arrangement, the compromise or arrangement shall, if sanctioned by the Tribunal, be binding on all the creditors or partners and the LLP.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 11 - Incorporation Document & Registered Office
question: Under Section 11 of the LLP Act, 2008, which of the following statements regarding the Incorporation Document is INCORRECT?
options: The statement required to be filed along with the incorporation document can only be signed by an advocate; CAs and CSs are not authorized.
Two or more persons associated for carrying on a lawful business with a view to profit must subscribe their names to an incorporation document.
The incorporation document shall be filed in such manner and with such fees as may be prescribed with the Registrar.
The document must state the name of the LLP and the proposed business.
ref: Section 11(1)(c) of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008
explanation: Under Section 11(1)(c), the statement shall be signed by an advocate, or by a Chartered Accountant or a Cost Accountant or a Company Secretary in practice, who is engaged in the formation of the LLP, and by anyone who subscribed his name to the incorporation document. Thus, CAs and CSs are fully authorized, making statement (a) incorrect.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 67 - Application of Companies Act Provisions to LLP
question: Does the Central Government have power to direct that any of the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 shall apply to any Limited Liability Partnership?
options: Yes, under Section 67(1), the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, direct that any of the provisions of the Companies Act shall apply to any LLP with such exception, modification and adaptation.
No, the LLP Act is a completely closed code and no provisions of the Companies Act can ever apply.
Yes, but only if the Supreme Court issues a writ of mandamus.
Only provisions relating to criminal trials apply automatically.
ref: Section 67(1) of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008
explanation: Under Section 67(1), the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, direct that any of the provisions of the Companies Act specified in the notification shall apply to any LLP or shall apply to any LLP with such exception, modification and adaptation as may be specified in the notification.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Small LLP Classification (LLP Amendment Act 2021)
question: Under the LLP (Amendment) Act, 2021, what are the statutory thresholds for an LLP to be classified as a 'Small LLP'?
options: Contribution does not exceed ₹25 Lakhs (or prescribed up to ₹5 Cr) AND turnover for the immediately preceding financial year does not exceed ₹40 Lakhs (or prescribed up to ₹50 Cr).
Contribution does not exceed ₹10 Lakhs and turnover does not exceed ₹20 Lakhs.
Contribution does not exceed ₹1 Crore with no turnover limit.
Small LLP status applies only if all partners are women.
ref: Section 2(1)(ta) of LLP Act, 2008 inserted by LLP (Amendment) Act, 2021
explanation: Under Section 2(1)(ta), 'small limited liability partnership' means an LLP: (i) the contribution of which does not exceed ₹25 Lakhs (or up to ₹5 Cr as prescribed); and (ii) the turnover of which for the immediately preceding financial year does not exceed ₹40 Lakhs (or up to ₹50 Cr as prescribed). Small LLPs enjoy lower compliance and penalty burdens.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 13 - Registered Office of LLP & Change of Place
question: Sunrise Agro LLP desires to shift its registered office from the State of Maharashtra to the State of Karnataka. What is the statutory requirement under Section 13 read with Rule 17?
options: Obtain the consent of all partners, prior consent of all secured creditors, and publish a notice in two national newspapers, followed by filing Form 15 with ROC.
Only an ordinary resolution passed by majority partners without notice to creditors.
Approval of the Central Government through Ministry of Corporate Affairs after a public hearing.
Registered office cannot be shifted from one state to another under the LLP Act.
ref: Section 13(3) of LLP Act 2008 read with Rule 17 of LLP Rules, 2009
explanation: Under Rule 17, where the change of place of registered office is from one State to another, the LLP must: (a) obtain consent of all partners unless agreement provides otherwise; (b) obtain prior written consent of all secured creditors; (c) publish notice in English and vernacular newspaper; and (d) file notice with the Registrar within 30 days in Form 15.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Sec 36 - Inspection of Documents at ROC
question: Under Section 36 of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, which of the following documents filed with the Registrar are open to public inspection by any person on payment of the prescribed fees?
options: Incorporation document, names of partners and changes therein, Statement of Account and Solvency, and Annual Return.
Internal minutes of meetings of partners only.
Confidential tax assessment orders and personal bank statements of partners.
No documents of an LLP are accessible to the public under any circumstances.
ref: Section 36 of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008
explanation: Under Section 36, the incorporation document, names of partners and changes therein, Statement of Account and Solvency, and annual return filed by an LLP with the Registrar shall be available for inspection by any person in the business hours of the Registrar on payment of prescribed fees.
